messages.subject: Beta version that displays errors
messages.subject_clean: Beta version that displays errors
messages.body_plain:
Hello Rhipe users,

Would you like to try a beta version that brings errors back to the R console
in an (I feel) easier to consume fashion?

After installing, try

library(Rhipe)

rhinit()
z=rhmr(map=expression({foo}),N=10,inout=c("lap","seq"),ofolder="/tmp/temporary",mapred=list(mapred.map.tasks=2,mapred.reduce.tasks=0))
f <- rhex(z,async=TRUE)
b <- rhstatus(f,mon.sec=5)
b

Since 'foo' is not present, this should throw an error.

Download: http://ml.stat.purdue.edu/rhipe/tmp/Rhipe_0.65.1.tar.gz

Cheers

Saptarshi

P.S The code hasn't been committed to Github nor is this version on the website.

messages.body_plain:
This was my response. I should point running rhcollect for i in 1:N is
not needed.
E.g. if F(i) is a real number and the trial id is not important, you could

rhcollect(1, unlist(lapply(map.values, F)) )

the 1 is just dummy. When this data is read back, you'll get

[1]
[[1]] 1
[[2]] F(1) F(2) .....

[2]]
[[1]] 1
[[2]] F(100) F(101) ....

This is very useful if you have millions of trials. Reading in
millions of keys,values (as would be the case if one follows the
example below)
would take very long time.

If the trial # is needed, you could do
rhcollect(1,
     do.call("rbind", lapply(map.values,function(r){
            c( r, F(r) )})) )

Some tips to make your experience better.

Saptarshi

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

The PDF doc is very old. The website now has the new one.
http://www.stat.purdue.edu/~sguha/rhipe/doc/RHIPE.pdf

Also, to answer the question below, here is my response.

## Suppose your input file is of the form (to create a text file of
numbers, see [1])

## N_11 N_12 N_13  .... N_1K
## ....

## ...
## N_p1 N_p2 N_p3 ....  N_pK

## You want to compute the mean and sd (is ro == correlation?)  For
this (and let's
## forget about numerical accuracy), we need the sums and sum of
squares of the K
## columns. Using that you can compute mean and sd.

map <- expression({
  ## K is the number of colums
  ## the number of rows is the length of map.values
  ## map.values is a list of lines
  ## this approach is okay, if you want /all/ the columns
  K <- 10
  l <- length(map.values)
  all.lines <- as.numeric(unlist(strsplit(unlist(map.values),"[[:space:]]+")))
  dim(all.lines) <- c(l, K) ## K is the number of columns
  sums <- apply(all.lines, 2, sum) ##by columns
  sqs <- apply(all.lines,2, function(r) sum(r^2)) # by columns
  sapply(1:K, function(r) rhcollect(r, c(l,sums[r],sqs[r])))
})

reduce <- expression(
  pre = { totals <- c(0,0,0)},
  reduce = { totals <-  totals + apply(do.call('rbind', reduce.values),2,sum) },
  post = {rhcollect(reduce.key,totals) }
)

## the mapred bit is optional, but if you have K columns, why run more reducers?
mr <- list(mapred.reduce.tasks=K)
y <- rhmr(map=map,
reduce=reduce,combiner=TRUE,inout=c("text","sequence"),ifolder="/tmp/somenumbers",
ofolder="/tmp/means",mapred=mr)
w <- rhex(y,async=TRUE)
z <- rhstatus(w, mon.sec=5)
results <- if(z$state=="SUCCEEDED") rhread("/tmp/means") else NULL
if(!is.null(results)){
  results <- cbind(unlist(lapply(results,"[[",1)),
                   do.call('rbind',lapply(results,"[[",2)))
  colnames(results) <- c("col.num","n","sum","ssq")
}

Cheers
Saptarshi

********************************************************************
[1] * How to make your text file with random numbers
*********************************************************************

make.numbers <- function(N,dest,cols=5,factor=1,local=FALSE){
  ## p is how long the word will be, longer more unique words
  ## factor, if equal to 1, then exactly N rows, otherwise N*factor rows
  ## cols how many columns per row
  map <- as.expression(bquote({
    COLS <- .(COLS)
    F <- .(F)
    lapply(map.values,function(r){
      for(i in 1:F){
        f <- runif(COLS)
        rhcollect(NULL,f)
      }
    })
  },list(COLS=cols,F=factor)))
  mapred <- list()
  if (local) mapred$mapred.job.tracker <- 'local'
  mapred[['mapred.field.separator']]=" "
  mapred[['mapred.textoutputformat.usekey']]=FALSE
  mapred$mapred.reduce.tasks=0
  z <- rhmr(map=map, N=N,ofolder=dest,inout=c("lapp","text"),
       mapred=mapred)
  rhex(z)
}

make.numbers(N=1000, "/tmp/somenumbers",cols=10)
## read them in (don't if N is too large!)
f <- rhread("/tmp/somenumbers/", type="text")

Hi,

Probably an installation issue.

a) Do you have permissions to run local jobs? Then try

 z=rhmr(map=m,reduce=r,comb=T,inout=c("text","sequence"),ifolder="/root/test1",ofolder='/root/out')

 rhex(z,mapred=list(mapred.job.tracker='local'))

b) Also, on the worker nodes try this

R_HOME=/ln/meraki/custom/lib64/R/ RHIPEWHAT=0 RHIPELOGFILE="/tmp/x"
rhipe_outputformat_class=foo rhipe_combiner=0
/ln/meraki/custom/lib64/R/library/Rhipe/libs/imperious.so

Does (b) work (i.e does it )?

Change R_HOME (you can get it by typing R.home() in R) and change the
path of imperious to where Rhipe is located
R
library(Rhipe)
rhoptions()$runner[1]

Saptarshi

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
First of , don't use rhlapply. It has been removed and was the distributed
version of lapply - so it did not take any input folder (as far as i recall), if
it did it would only take sequence file input format not text file.

For your problem below, use rhmr, specifying the input folder with text files
and use text/sequence output format.

> 1. Sequence along the characters from "a" to "z",which are my keys.
> 2. For each character grep all the words in which the character is
> appearing. For this i am using R grep() function. These vector of
> words would be my "values" to the keys.
> For example:
>  for key "a" the values could be "and", "bad", "amazon" etc
> for key "b" the values could be "bad", "boss" etc.. (Note there would
> be duplication of words)
>

So your map would look like

map <- expression({
  lines.of.text <- unlist(strsplit(unlist(map.values),"[[:space:]]+"))
  counts <- sapply(letters,function(alpha){
    value <- lines.of.text[grep(alpha, lines.of.text)]
    if(length(value)==0) value <- ''
    rhcollect(alpha,value)
  })
})

mapred <- list(mapred.reduce.tasks=0, mapred.field.separator="
",mapred.job.tracker='local')
z <- rhmr(map=map, ifolder=path-to-input,ofolder="/tmp/job",
     inout=c("text","text"),mapred=mapred)
rhex(z)

(You need the if(length(value)==0 bit, for text output. RHIPE throws an
indexoutofbounds  exception when trying to strinfigy a vector of length  0. For
sequence file output, it is not needed, the return value be an empty
character vector)

Hope this helps

Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] GREP application on Hadoop using RHIPE
messages.subject_clean: [rhipe] GREP application on Hadoop using RHIPE
messages.body_plain:
I should also point out that those values (vectors) could potentially
be very large!

Since you already have a case where you might get multiple lines for
the same key( since each
map task will potentially write a value for the key 'a' and there is
no reducer), you
might as well split long values and write them out as multiple lines.
RHIPE has a cap on value length i think its 128MB or 256MB.

The following code doesn't do that. It instead, partitions by key
(values for same letter in one file) and sorts within part file (by
key)

map <- expression({
  lines.of.text <- unlist(strsplit(unlist(map.values),"[[:space:]]+"))
  counts <- sapply(letters,function(alpha){
    value <- lines.of.text[grep(alpha, lines.of.text)]
    if(length(value)==0) value <- ''
    rhcollect(alpha,value)
  })
})

reduce <- expression(
    reduce = { lapply(reduce.values,function(r) rhcollect(reduce.key,r)) }
    )

mapred <- list(mapred.field.separator=" ")
z <- rhmr(map=map,reduce=reduce, ifolder=filename,ofolder="/tmp/job",
     inout=c("text","text"),orderby="char",mapred=mapred,part=list(lims=1,type='string'))
rhex(z)

This can take time, e.g. for 2.8GB data read (100MM records, 5 words
per line), 14GB was written (867,984 records)
and it took 13 minutes (72 cores, 8 computers, 5 TB of space)

BTW, the reducer is an identity reducer, but if you use the 'orderby'
parameter, you *have* to provide an R reducer.
Saptarshi

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Not surprising. The map potentially emits multiple records for a given letter of
the alphabet (key). So your part files have multiple records for a key.

Using map file output format won't help you in this case (you'll only get the
first).

1. Compute a count of the number of records for a given letter of the alphabet.
   map --> (letter[i], 1)
   reduce ---> expression(
         pre = { total <- 0 },
         reduce = { total <- total+ sum(unlist(reduce.values)) },
         post = { rhcollect(reduce.key, total) }
    )

2. Also, using partitioner=list(lims=1, type='string') and
   mapred.reduce.tasks=27 will create 27 part files, each key (letter of the
   alphabet) being places in its own table.

Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Size of the data frame in created in RHIPE
messages.subject_clean: [rhipe] Size of the data frame in created in RHIPE
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

The maximum size of any key/value is 128MB. But you should not rely on that,
keep your keys/values as small as possible (< 2MB). RHIPE (and this is not a
good design in retrospect, will be fixed soon) loads in rhipe_map_buffsize
number of key,value pairs at one time (the length of map.values and map.keys),
and so if the average size of a value is 2MB, then the default of value of
rhipe_map_buffsize (5000) will use up 10GB!

So you'll always need to specify a small size of rhipe_map_buffsize. Data frame
sizes depend on the number of columns and type of the column. But size is not
the only issue. In the airline data set each data frame had somewhere around 2K
rows. The size was not large (< 100 KB ) but rhipe_map_buffsize was not changed
from the default, the example code would be rbind-ing  2K*5K == 10MM rows which
would take forever.

So if you have 5 MM rows, store each as data frames of e.g. 2000 rows and
forever specify a small value of rhipe_map_buffsize and do your computations
across blocks of data frames.

Cheers
Saptarshi

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Output files creation in map reduce job
messages.subject_clean: [rhipe] Output files creation in map reduce job
messages.body_plain:
On Thu, Dec 30, 2010 at 5:27 AM, Sphinx <hr.profe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi ,
> I would like to know how to determine the number of output files to be
> generated.

If mapred.reduce.tasks=0, the number of output files is the number of
tasks as defined by the
inputformat. E.g. for a sequence file input format, it is the number
of blocks of all the input files.
So a 1GB file stored as 128MB blocks would create 8 (1GB/128MB == 8)
tasks and therefore 8 files.

if mapred.reduce.tasks >0, there will be mapred.reduce.task number of
files, though some might be empty.

Whether you need mapred.reduce.task >0 or not depends on your needs.

> with one output file, yeah i do agree with the fact that hadoop will
> split those files into blocks of data and will distribute across the
> nodes.
>

Answered above.
